title: Alarms, Trends, Environmental Records and Shift Handoff

content.overview: Environmental work is not complete when a technician reads a dashboard. Learners practice distinguishing instantaneous values, trends, averages and alarms; documenting verification actions; connecting readings to crop location and equipment context; and producing a shift handoff that makes unresolved environmental or lighting conditions reconstructable without hiding uncertainty.

vocabulary.definition: A sequence of measurements over time used to identify direction, cycling, transitions or recurring patterns.
A system or procedural indication that a defined condition or rule has been met and requires a specified response.
A value that differs substantially from comparison values or the surrounding pattern and therefore warrants context or verification.
A structured transfer of completed checks, observations, deviations, unresolved conditions and priorities to the next responsible person.

sections.title: Instantaneous values, averages and trends answer different questions
sections.body: A current value shows one moment, an average summarizes a period and a trend preserves change over time. Equipment cycling, lights-on/off transitions or short excursions can disappear inside averages, so technicians use the form of data required by the task instead of treating every summary as interchangeable.

sections.title: An alarm is evidence of a rule event, not a diagnosis
sections.body: When an alarm occurs, record the alarm identity, affected room or asset, time, relevant readings and the permitted verification actions. The alarm may indicate a threshold or system condition, but it does not by itself establish biological damage or root cause.

sections.title: Handoffs preserve unresolved conditions
sections.body: A useful handoff states what was observed, what target or limit applied, what checks were completed, what remained unresolved, who was notified and what follow-up is required. If data quality is uncertain, the uncertainty is part of the handoff rather than being replaced with a guessed value or cause.

workedExamples: A daily temperature average appears normal, but the trend shows a repeated lights-on spike. The technician records the recurring transition pattern and escalates under the supplied procedure rather than reporting only the average.

A photoperiod alarm is cleared after an authorized status check, but the cause is not established. The handoff records the alarm, observed controller/light state, check performed and unresolved cause.
commonMistakes: Using a daily average to dismiss short repeated excursions.
Writing an alarm as a confirmed diagnosis or equipment root cause.
Closing a handoff with “fixed” when only the alarm was acknowledged and the cause remains unresolved.
Backfilling a missed reading from memory as though it were measured at the scheduled time.
content.practicalApplication: Review a simulated 24-hour environmental/light trend with one sensor outlier and one alarm. Identify the important event, record the target versus measured values, document permitted verification, and create a receiving-shift handoff that clearly separates resolved actions from unresolved cause or data-quality questions.
content.summary: Environmental records need time, location, measurement and equipment context. Trends and alarms support investigation but do not automatically prove cause. Technician I verifies within procedure, records uncertainty honestly and hands off unresolved conditions so the next qualified person can continue the work.

blocks.title: Environmental deviation handoff
blocks.description: A reconstructable handoff separates evidence, checks and unresolved work.

fields.label: Time window
fields.value: When the reading, trend or alarm occurred

fields.label: Target/limit
fields.value: Supplied target or alarm rule applicable to the task

fields.label: Observed evidence
fields.value: Measured values, trend, photoperiod/light state or alarm identity

fields.label: Unresolved condition
fields.value: What is still unknown or outside technician authority

fields.label: Escalation
fields.value: Who was notified and according to which process

fields.label: Next action
fields.value: Required follow-up for the receiving role

blocks.title: Average hides a repeated spike
blocks.setting: The 24-hour average temperature is within the supplied range, but the trend shows a short spike at each lights-on transition.
options: Document the repeated transition spike with time/location context and escalate if the supplied procedure requires it
Delete the spikes because they are brief
Independently change HVAC controls without authorization
blocks.answer: Document the repeated transition spike with time/location context and escalate if the supplied procedure requires it
blocks.feedback: Averages can conceal meaningful dynamics. The trend should be preserved without assuming root cause or exceeding role authority.
